## Base rates by position

Measured over **players actually drafted in rounds 1-8 of this league** — the population that was expected to start. Using all fantasy-relevant player-seasons instead put QB at 10.3 games, which is not an injury rate: it is backup quarterbacks clearing a per-game threshold across a handful of starts.

| RB | 166 | **13.95** | 15 | 48% | 19% |
| WR | 168 | **14.23** | 16 | 51% | 17% |
| TE | 28 | **14.07** | 15 | 39% | 21% |

## Manager injury luck

Games missed by the players each manager **drafted**, over the seasons for which player-level data exists (2021–2025). Restricted to each manager's first eight picks — the ones intended as starters — so that late fliers do not dominate.

Expected games per drafted starter, by position (the reference population is drafted starters themselves, not all NFL contributors): **QB** 14.77, **RB** 13.95, **TE** 14.07, **WR** 14.23.

| manager | picks | expected | actual | delta | per pick | ± SE | t |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Matt McCauley | 39 | 550 | 517 | **-34** | -0.86 | 0.60 | -1.43 |
| James Galante | 40 | 566 | 534 | **-32** | -0.81 | 0.63 | -1.28 |
| Bryan Cannon | 40 | 565 | 559 | **-6** | -0.14 | 0.58 | -0.24 |
| Brendan Gamble | 40 | 567 | 564 | **-3** | -0.07 | 0.47 | -0.14 |
| Brian Dzuris | 40 | 566 | 571 | **+5** | +0.12 | 0.65 | +0.18 |
| Donnie Darco | 40 | 564 | 569 | **+5** | +0.12 | 0.62 | +0.19 |
| Anthony Lettieri | 40 | 567 | 577 | **+10** | +0.26 | 0.49 | +0.53 |
| Jonathan Wiggins | 40 | 566 | 577 | **+11** | +0.29 | 0.51 | +0.56 |
| Stephen Rogers | 40 | 568 | 582 | **+14** | +0.36 | 0.49 | +0.73 |
| Tyler Clark | 38 | 538 | 568 | **+30** | +0.78 | 0.43 | +1.82 |

Range: **Matt McCauley** -0.86 games per drafted starter, **Tyler Clark** +0.78. Over eight starters that is a spread of 13.1 games a season between the unluckiest and the luckiest.

### None of this is statistically significant

The largest t-statistic in the table is **1.82**. With ~40 drafted starters per manager over five seasons, and a standard deviation of roughly five games on any single player's availability, the standard error on these per-pick figures is ~0.5 games — comparable to the effects themselves. **Nobody in this room is measurably lucky or unlucky with injuries.**

That is a more useful answer than a ranking would be. The ordering is real in the sense that it happened, but it does not predict anything, and it should not be carried into 2026 as a belief about anyone's fortune — including one's own. Five seasons is simply too few.

**What IS actionable** is the per-player table above. Individual durability is measured on far more data than a manager's forty picks, and it is the input the draft can actually use: prefer the durable player when value is close, and price the fragile one down rather than hoping. With no IR slot, a player who misses six games costs a roster spot as well as the points.

Note also that drafting fragile players and being unlucky are indistinguishable in this table by construction. If a manager were persistently negative across many more seasons, the actionable reading would be that he keeps buying injury risk — not that the universe dislikes him.
